141: static int audio_dma_getcaps(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, int type,
142:                              struct audio_caps_s *caps)
143: {
144:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
145: 
146:   /* Validate the structure */
147: 
148:   DEBUGASSERT(caps && caps->ac_len >= sizeof(struct audio_caps_s));
149:   audinfo("type=%d ac_type=%d\n", type, caps->ac_type);
150: 
151:   /* Fill in the caller's structure based on requested info */
152: 
153:   caps->ac_format.hw  = 0;
154:   caps->ac_controls.w = 0;
155: 
156:   switch (caps->ac_type)
157:     {
158:       /* Caller is querying for the types of units we support */
159: 
160:       case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:
161: 
162:         /* Provide our overall capabilities.  The interfacing software
163:          * must then call us back for specific info for each capability.
164:          */
165: 
166:         caps->ac_channels = 2;       /* Stereo output */
167: 
168:         if (caps->ac_subtype == AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY)
169:           {
170:               /* We don't decode any formats!  Only something above us in
171:                * the audio stream can perform decoding on our behalf.
172:                */
173: 
174:               /* The types of audio units we implement */
175: 
176:               if (audio_dma->playback)
177:               {
178:                 caps->ac_controls.b[0] = AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT;
179:               }
180:               else
181:               {
182:                 caps->ac_controls.b[0] = AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT;
183:               }
184: 
185:               caps->ac_format.hw = 1 << (AUDIO_FMT_PCM - 1);
186:           }
187: 
188:         caps->ac_controls.b[0] = AUDIO_SUBFMT_END;
189:         break;
190: 
191:         /* Provide capabilities of our OUTPUT unit */
192: 
193:       case AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT:
194:       case AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT:
195: 
196:         caps->ac_channels = 2;
197: 
198:         if (caps->ac_subtype == AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY)
199:           {
200:             /* Report the Sample rates we support */
201: 
202:               caps->ac_controls.hw[0] = AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_DEF_ALL;
203:           }
204: 
205:         break;
206:    }
207: 
208:   /* Return the length of the audio_caps_s struct for validation of
209:    * proper Audio device type.
210:    */
211: 
212:   return caps->ac_len;
213: }
214: 
215: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
216: static int audio_dma_configure(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
217:                                void *session,
218:                                const struct audio_caps_s *caps)
219: #else
220: static int audio_dma_configure(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
221:                                const struct audio_caps_s *caps)
222: #endif
223: {
224:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
225:   struct dma_config_s cfg;
226:   int ret = -EINVAL;
227: 
228:   DEBUGASSERT(audio_dma && caps);
229:   audinfo("ac_type: %d\n", caps->ac_type);
230: 
231:   /* Process the configure operation */
232: 
233:   switch (caps->ac_type)
234:     {
235:       case AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT:
236:         if (audio_dma->playback)
237:           {
238:             memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(struct dma_config_s));
239:             cfg.direction = DMA_MEM_TO_DEV;
240:             if (audio_dma->fifo_width)
241:               cfg.dst_width = audio_dma->fifo_width;
242:             else
243:               cfg.dst_width = caps->ac_controls.b[2] / 8;
244:             ret = DMA_CONFIG(audio_dma->chan, &cfg);
245:           }
246:         break;
247:       case AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT:
248:         if (!audio_dma->playback)
249:           {
250:             memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(struct dma_config_s));
251:             cfg.direction = DMA_DEV_TO_MEM;
252:             if (audio_dma->fifo_width)
253:               cfg.src_width = audio_dma->fifo_width;
254:             else
255:               cfg.src_width = caps->ac_controls.b[2] / 8;
256:             ret = DMA_CONFIG(audio_dma->chan, &cfg);
257:           }
258:         break;
259:       default:
260:         ret = -ENOTTY;
261:         break;
262:     }
263: 
264:   return ret;
265: }

267: static int audio_dma_shutdown(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
268: {
269:   /* apps enqueued buffers, but doesn't start. stop here to
270:    * clear audio_dma->pendq.
271:    */
272: 
273: #ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_STOP
274: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
275:   audio_dma_stop(dev, NULL);
276: #else
277:   audio_dma_stop(dev);
278: #endif
279: #endif
280: 
281:   return OK;
282: }
283: 
284: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
285: static int audio_dma_start(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, void *session)
286: #else
287: static int audio_dma_start(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
288: #endif
289: {
290:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
291: 
292:   return DMA_START_CYCLIC(audio_dma->chan, audio_dma_callback, audio_dma,
293:                           audio_dma->dst_addr, audio_dma->src_addr,
294:                           audio_dma->buffer_num * audio_dma->buffer_size,
295:                           audio_dma->buffer_size);
296: }
297: 
298: #ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_STOP
299: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
300: static int audio_dma_stop(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, void *session)
301: #else
302: static int audio_dma_stop(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
303: #endif
304: {
305:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
306:   struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
307: 
308:   DMA_STOP(audio_dma->chan);
309: 
310:   while (!dq_empty(&audio_dma->pendq))
311:     {
312:       apb = (struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_remfirst(&audio_dma->pendq);
313: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
314:       audio_dma->dev.upper(audio_dma->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE,
315:                            apb, OK, NULL);
316: #else
317:       audio_dma->dev.upper(audio_dma->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE,
318:                            apb, OK);
319: #endif
320:     }
321: 
322: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
323:   audio_dma->dev.upper(audio_dma->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_COMPLETE,
324:                        NULL, OK, NULL);
325: #else
326:   audio_dma->dev.upper(audio_dma->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_COMPLETE,
327:                        NULL, OK);
328: #endif
329:   audio_dma->xrun = false;
330:   return OK;
331: }
332: #endif
333: 
334: #ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_PAUSE_RESUME
335: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
336: static int audio_dma_pause(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, void *session)
337: #else
338: static int audio_dma_pause(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
339: #endif
340: {
341:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
342: 
343:   return DMA_PAUSE(audio_dma->chan);
344: }
345: 
346: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
347: static int audio_dma_resume(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, void *session)
348: #else
349: static int audio_dma_resume(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
350: #endif
351: {
352:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
353: 
354:   if (dq_empty(&audio_dma->pendq))
355:     {
356:       return -EINVAL;
357:     }
358: 
359:   return DMA_RESUME(audio_dma->chan);
360: }
361: #endif
362: 
363: static int audio_dma_allocbuffer(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
364:                                  struct audio_buf_desc_s *bufdesc)
365: {
366:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
367:   struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
368: 
369:   if (bufdesc->numbytes != audio_dma->buffer_size)
370:     {
371:       return -EINVAL;
372:     }
373: 
374:   if (audio_dma->alloc_index == audio_dma->buffer_num)
375:     {
376:       return -ENOMEM;
377:     }
378: 
379:   if (!audio_dma->alloc_addr)
380:     {
381:       audio_dma->alloc_addr = kumm_memalign(32,
382:                                             audio_dma->buffer_num *
383:                                             audio_dma->buffer_size);
384:       if (!audio_dma->alloc_addr)
385:         {
386:           return -ENOMEM;
387:         }
388: 
389:       if (audio_dma->playback)
390:         audio_dma->src_addr = up_addrenv_va_to_pa(audio_dma->alloc_addr);
391:       else
392:         audio_dma->dst_addr = up_addrenv_va_to_pa(audio_dma->alloc_addr);
393:     }
394: 
395:   apb = kumm_zalloc(sizeof(struct ap_buffer_s));
396:   *bufdesc->u.pbuffer = apb;
397: 
398:   /* Test if the allocation was successful or not */
399: 
400:   if (*bufdesc->u.pbuffer == NULL)
401:     {
402:       return -ENOMEM;
403:     }
404: 
405:   /* Populate the buffer contents */
406: 
407:   apb->i.channels = 2;
408:   apb->crefs      = 1;
409:   apb->nmaxbytes  = audio_dma->buffer_size;
410:   apb->samp = audio_dma->alloc_addr +
411:               audio_dma->alloc_index *
412:               audio_dma->buffer_size;
413:   audio_dma->alloc_index++;
414:   nxmutex_init(&apb->lock);
415: 
416:   return sizeof(struct audio_buf_desc_s);
417: }
418: 
419: static int audio_dma_freebuffer(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
420:                                 struct audio_buf_desc_s *bufdesc)
421: {
422:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
423:   struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
424: 
425:   apb = bufdesc->u.buffer;
426:   audio_dma->alloc_index--;
427:   nxmutex_destroy(&apb->lock);
428:   kumm_free(apb);
429: 
430:   if (audio_dma->alloc_index == 0)
431:     {
432:       kumm_free(audio_dma->alloc_addr);
433:       audio_dma->alloc_addr = NULL;
434:     }
435: 
436:   return sizeof(struct audio_buf_desc_s);
437: }
438: 
439: static int audio_dma_enqueuebuffer(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
440:                                    struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
441: {
442:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
443:   irqstate_t flags;
444: 
445:   if (audio_dma->playback)
446:     up_clean_dcache((uintptr_t)apb->samp,
447:                     (uintptr_t)apb->samp + apb->nbytes);
448: 
449:   apb->flags |= AUDIO_APB_OUTPUT_ENQUEUED;
450: 
451:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&audio_dma->lock);
452:   dq_addlast(&apb->dq_entry, &audio_dma->pendq);
453:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&audio_dma->lock, flags);
454: 
455:   if (audio_dma->xrun)
456:     {
457:       audio_dma->xrun = false;
458:       return audio_dma_resume(dev);
459:     }
460: 
461:   return OK;
462: }
463: 
464: static int audio_dma_ioctl(struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
465:                            unsigned long arg)
466: {
467:   struct audio_dma_s *audio_dma = (struct audio_dma_s *)dev;
468:   struct ap_buffer_info_s *bufinfo;
469: 
470:   switch (cmd)
471:     {
472:       /* Report our preferred buffer size and quantity */
473: 
474:       case AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:
475:         audinfo("AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:\n");
476:         bufinfo              = (struct ap_buffer_info_s *)arg;
477:         bufinfo->buffer_size = audio_dma->buffer_size;
478:         bufinfo->nbuffers    = audio_dma->buffer_num;
479: 
480:         return OK;
481: 
482:       case AUDIOIOC_SETBUFFERINFO:
483:         audinfo("AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:\n");
484:         bufinfo                = (struct ap_buffer_info_s *)arg;
485:         audio_dma->buffer_size = bufinfo->buffer_size;
486:         audio_dma->buffer_num  = bufinfo->nbuffers;
487:         kumm_free(audio_dma->alloc_addr);
488:         audio_dma->alloc_addr = NULL;
489:         audio_dma->alloc_index = 0;
490: 
491:         return OK;
492:     }
493: 
494:   return -ENOTTY;
495: }

497: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION

499: #else

501: #endif

504: }
505: 
506: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION

510: #endif

513: }

122: #define BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_MASK          0x1fu
123: #define BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_SRC_SEC       (1u << 20)
124: #define BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_DEST_SEC      (1u << 21)
125: 
126: #define BK7258_DMA_STATUS_REMAIN_LEN_MASK 0x1ffffu
127: #define BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FLUSH_SRC_BUFF  (1u << 17)
128: #define BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FINISH_INT      (1u << 18)

130: /* Spin bound for the source-buffer flush.  The flush drains at most one
131:  * data-width unit, so it completes in a handful of bus cycles; the bound is
132:  * only here so a wedged bus cannot hang an interrupt handler forever.
133:  */
134: 
135: #define BK7258_DMA_FLUSH_TIMEOUT     1000u

137: /****************************************************************************
138:  * Private Data
139:  ****************************************************************************/
140: 
141: static bk7258_dma_done_cb_t g_done_cb[BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS];
142: static void *g_done_cb_arg[BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS];

144: /****************************************************************************
145:  * Private Functions
146:  ****************************************************************************/
147: 
148: /****************************************************************************
149:  * Name: bk7258_dma_isr
150:  *
151:  * Description:
152:  *   Services every channel that has a callback registered.  Scanning is
153:  *   used rather than the global int_status word because channel-to-interrupt
154:  *   line assignment goes through the int_allocate register, which this
155:  *   driver leaves at its reset value; the per-channel finish_int bit is
156:  *   unambiguous either way, and with one active channel the scan is a
157:  *   handful of register reads.
158:  *
159:  *   A SINGLE-mode channel is disabled once it completes, matching what this
160:  *   driver has always done: a stale "finish" state would otherwise confuse
161:  *   the next configure().  A REPEAT-mode channel is left running -- that is
162:  *   the whole point of REPEAT, and its finish interrupt is a progress
163:  *   report, not an end.
164:  *
165:  *   Interrupt context: no printf, no allocation, no blocking.
166:  *
167:  ****************************************************************************/
168: 
169: static int bk7258_dma_isr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
170: {
171:   unsigned int ch;
172: 
173:   for (ch = 0; ch < BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS; ch++)
174:     {
175:       uint32_t status;
176: 
177:       if (g_done_cb[ch] == NULL)
178:         {
179:           continue;
180:         }
181: 
182:       status = getreg32(BK7258_DMA_CH_STATUS(ch));
183:       if ((status & BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FINISH_INT) == 0)
184:         {
185:           continue;
186:         }
187: 
188:       /* Write-1-to-clear, and only that bit: the low half of this register
189:        * is the read-only remain_len, and the neighbouring interrupt bits are
190:        * W1C too, so a read-modify-write would clear whichever of them
191:        * happened to be pending.
192:        */
193: 
194:       putreg32(BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FINISH_INT, BK7258_DMA_CH_STATUS(ch));
195: 
196:       if ((getreg32(BK7258_DMA_CH_CTRL(ch)) & BK7258_DMA_CTRL_MODE_MASK) ==
197:           BK7258_DMA_CTRL_MODE_SINGLE)
198:         {
199:           modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CH_CTRL(ch), BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
200:         }
201: 
202:       g_done_cb[ch](g_done_cb_arg[ch]);
203:     }
204: 
205:   return 0;
206: }

209:  * Public Functions
210:  ****************************************************************************/

212: /****************************************************************************
213:  * Name: bk7258_dma_init
214:  *
215:  * Description:
216:  *   Brings up the DMA unit, then attaches its interrupt.
217:  *
218:  *   The unit-level work here was missing while this driver had no callers,
219:  *   and it is not optional -- a channel programmed without it is configured
220:  *   correctly and moves nothing:
221:  *
222:  *     - soft_reset must be released.  As with YUV_BUF, the bit reads as
223:  *       "released" when it is 1, so the reset value of 0 means the unit is
224:  *       held in reset (dma_ll_init(): prio_mode.v = 0 then soft_reset = 1).
225:  *     - secure_attr and privileged_attr are per-channel bitmaps, and this AP
226:  *       runs in the secure world (CONFIG_ARCH_TRUSTZONE_SECURE=y, hence the
227:  *       -mcmse in its compile flags).  The reference opens all twelve
228:  *       channels in both maps under CONFIG_SPE; leaving them at zero leaves
229:  *       the channel unable to access secure memory, with no error reported
230:  *       anywhere.
231:  *     - prio_mode round-robin matches dma_hal_init().
232:  *
233:  ****************************************************************************/
234: 
235: void bk7258_dma_init(void)
236: {
237:   putreg32(BK7258_DMA_PRIO_SOFT_RESET | BK7258_DMA_PRIO_MODE_RR,
238:            BK7258_DMA_PRIO_MODE);
239:   putreg32(BK7258_DMA_ATTR_ALL_CHANNELS, BK7258_DMA_SECURE_ATTR);
240:   putreg32(BK7258_DMA_ATTR_ALL_CHANNELS, BK7258_DMA_PRIV_ATTR);
241: 
242:   modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL, BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
243: 
244:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_DMA, bk7258_dma_isr, NULL);
245:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_DMA);
246: 
247:   printf("bk7258_dma: init: prio_mode=0x%08x secure_attr=0x%08x "
248:          "priv_attr=0x%08x irq=%d\n",
249:          (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_DMA_PRIO_MODE),
250:          (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_DMA_SECURE_ATTR),
251:          (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_DMA_PRIV_ATTR),
252:          (int)BK7258_IRQ_DMA);
253: }

255: void bk7258_dma_configure(uint32_t src_addr, uint32_t dest_addr,
256:                            uint32_t transfer_len)
257: {
258:   struct bk7258_dma_cfg_s cfg;
259: 
260:   /* Expressed through the general path so there is one implementation of
261:    * the register writes, with the memory-to-memory defaults spelled out.
262:    */
263: 
264:   cfg.channel         = BK7258_DMA_CHANNEL;
265:   cfg.src_addr        = src_addr;
266:   cfg.dest_addr       = dest_addr;
267:   cfg.transfer_len    = transfer_len;
268:   cfg.src_dev         = BK7258_DMA_DEV_MEM;
269:   cfg.dest_dev        = BK7258_DMA_DEV_MEM;
270:   cfg.src_inc         = true;
271:   cfg.dest_inc        = true;
272:   cfg.repeat          = false;
273:   cfg.dest_loop_start = 0;
274:   cfg.dest_loop_end   = 0;
275:   cfg.data_width      = BK7258_DMA_WIDTH_8BITS;
276: 
277:   bk7258_dma_configure_ex(&cfg);
278: }
279: 
280: int bk7258_dma_configure_ex(const struct bk7258_dma_cfg_s *cfg)
281: {
282:   uint32_t ctrl;
283:   uint32_t len_field;
284: 
285:   if (cfg == NULL || cfg->channel >= BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS ||
286:       cfg->transfer_len == 0 ||
287:       cfg->transfer_len > BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_MASK + 1u ||
288:       cfg->data_width > BK7258_DMA_WIDTH_32BITS)
289:     {
290:       return -1;
291:     }
292: 
293:   /* Disable before reprogramming source/dest/length. */
294: 
295:   modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CH_CTRL(cfg->channel),
296:               BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
297: 
298:   putreg32(cfg->src_addr, BK7258_DMA_CH_SRC_ADDR(cfg->channel));
299:   putreg32(cfg->dest_addr, BK7258_DMA_CH_DEST_ADDR(cfg->channel));
300: 
301:   /* Request lines, plus the security attribute of each endpoint.
302:    *
303:    * The value written for a device is the hardware's req_mux encoding, which
304:    * is NOT the position of the device in the vendor's dma_dev_t enum --
305:    * dma_ll_dev_to_req_mux() translates between them (JPEG is enum entry 28
306:    * but req_mux 0x19).  bk7258_dma.h therefore defines the encodings, not
307:    * the enum order.
308:    *
309:    * src_sec_attr/dest_sec_attr are set because this AP is the secure world;
310:    * the reference sets both for its JPEG channel under CONFIG_SPE
311:    * (bk_dma_set_src_sec_attr/bk_dma_set_dest_sec_attr in
312:    * dvp_camera_dma_config()).  Burst lengths are left at their reset value:
313:    * the reference's INC16 destination burst is a throughput choice, not a
314:    * requirement, and one variable at a time.
315:    */
316: 
317:   putreg32(((uint32_t)cfg->src_dev & BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_MASK) <<
318:              BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_SRC_SHIFT |
319:            ((uint32_t)cfg->dest_dev & BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_MASK) <<
320:              BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_DEST_SHIFT |
321:            BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_SRC_SEC | BK7258_DMA_REQ_MUX_DEST_SEC,
322:            BK7258_DMA_CH_REQ_MUX(cfg->channel));
323: 
324:   /* Circular destination, for a channel that has to keep writing past the
325:    * end of one transfer_len chunk without software touching it.
326:    */
327: 
328:   if (cfg->dest_loop_end > cfg->dest_loop_start)
329:     {
330:       putreg32(cfg->dest_loop_start,
331:                BK7258_DMA_CH_DEST_LOOP_START(cfg->channel));
332:       putreg32(cfg->dest_loop_end,
333:                BK7258_DMA_CH_DEST_LOOP_END(cfg->channel));
334:     }
335: 
336:   /* ctrl.transfer_len encodes (byte_count - 1). */
337: 
338:   len_field = (cfg->transfer_len - 1u) & BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_MASK;
339: 
340:   ctrl = BK7258_DMA_CTRL_FINISH_INT_EN |
341:          (cfg->repeat ? BK7258_DMA_CTRL_MODE_REPEAT :
342:                         BK7258_DMA_CTRL_MODE_SINGLE) |
343:          ((uint32_t)cfg->data_width << BK7258_DMA_CTRL_SRC_WIDTH_SHIFT) |
344:          ((uint32_t)cfg->data_width << BK7258_DMA_CTRL_DEST_WIDTH_SHIFT) |
345:          (len_field << BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_SHIFT);
346: 
347:   if (cfg->src_inc)
348:     {
349:       ctrl |= BK7258_DMA_CTRL_SRC_INC_EN;
350:     }
351: 
352:   if (cfg->dest_inc)
353:     {
354:       ctrl |= BK7258_DMA_CTRL_DEST_INC_EN;
355:     }
356: 
357:   if (cfg->dest_loop_end > cfg->dest_loop_start)
358:     {
359:       ctrl |= BK7258_DMA_CTRL_DEST_LOOP_EN;
360:     }
361: 
362:   putreg32(ctrl, BK7258_DMA_CH_CTRL(cfg->channel));
363: 
364:   return 0;
365: }

367: void bk7258_dma_set_done_callback(bk7258_dma_done_cb_t cb, void *arg)

369:   bk7258_dma_set_channel_callback(BK7258_DMA_CHANNEL, cb, arg);

372: void bk7258_dma_set_channel_callback(uint8_t channel,
373:                                      bk7258_dma_done_cb_t cb, void *arg)

375:   if (channel < BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS)

383:       g_done_cb[channel] = cb;

431:          BK7258_DMA_STATUS_REMAIN_LEN_MASK;

434: /****************************************************************************
435:  * Name: bk7258_dma_flush_src_buffer
436:  *
437:  * Description:
438:  *   Pushes out whatever partial data-width unit the channel is holding on
439:  *   its source side.
440:  *
441:  *   Needed at the end of a peripheral-sourced transfer: the last bytes of a
442:  *   JPEG frame are unlikely to land on a 32-bit boundary, and without this
443:  *   they sit in the channel and are counted as "not yet transferred", so the
444:  *   frame looks short by up to three bytes.
445:  *
446:  *   Only bit[17] is written, never a read-modify-write, for the reason given
447:  *   in the interrupt handler: the neighbouring interrupt bits are
448:  *   write-1-to-clear.  The poll is bounded so this stays safe to call from
449:  *   interrupt context.
450:  *
451:  ****************************************************************************/
452: 
453: void bk7258_dma_flush_src_buffer(uint8_t channel)
454: {
455:   unsigned int spins;
456: 
457:   if (channel >= BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS)
458:     {
459:       return;
460:     }
461: 
462:   putreg32(BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FLUSH_SRC_BUFF,
463:            BK7258_DMA_CH_STATUS(channel));
464: 
465:   for (spins = 0; spins < BK7258_DMA_FLUSH_TIMEOUT; spins++)
466:     {
467:       if ((getreg32(BK7258_DMA_CH_STATUS(channel)) &
468:            BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FLUSH_SRC_BUFF) == 0)
469:         {
470:           break;
471:         }
472:     }
473: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_dma.h
3:  *
4:  * BK7258 general DMA driver.
5:  *
6:  * Two interfaces:
7:  *
8:  *   bk7258_dma_configure() and friends
9:  *     Single-shot memory-to-memory on channel 0.  Unchanged; callers that
10:  *     only need a block copy keep working exactly as before.
11:  *
12:  *   bk7258_dma_configure_ex()
13:  *     Any channel, a peripheral at either end with hardware flow control,
14:  *     REPEAT mode, and a circular destination.  Needed by anything draining
15:  *     or feeding a FIFO: the hardware JPEG encoder's bitstream leaves only
16:  *     through a FIFO register, and the audio path wants to stop copying
17:  *     samples in its interrupt handler.
18:  *
19:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
20:  ****************************************************************************/
21: 
22: #ifndef __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_INCLUDE_BK7258_DMA_H
23: #define __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_INCLUDE_BK7258_DMA_H
24: 
25: #include <stdbool.h>
26: #include <stdint.h>
27: 
28: /****************************************************************************
29:  * Pre-processor Definitions
30:  ****************************************************************************/
31: 
32: /* Channels the unit has.  The controller's per-channel bitmask registers
33:  * (secure_attr, int_status0/1) are 12 bits wide, which is where this comes
34:  * from (dma_struct.h).
35:  */
36: 
37: #define BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS       12u
38: 
39: /* Peripheral request lines.
40:  *
41:  * These are the hardware's req_mux encodings, taken from
42:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/dma_reg.h (DMA_V_REQ_MUX_*).  They are
43:  * deliberately not the vendor's dma_dev_t enum values: that enum is an API
44:  * convenience and dma_ll_dev_to_req_mux() maps it onto these numbers.  JPEG,
45:  * for instance, is enum entry 28 but request line 0x19.  Getting this wrong
46:  * does not fail loudly -- the channel simply waits for a request that never
47:  * comes, or worse, responds to a different peripheral's.
48:  */
49: 
50: #define BK7258_DMA_DEV_MEM         0x00u   /* DMA_V_REQ_MUX_DTCM  */
51: #define BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_TX    0x0du   /* DMA_V_REQ_MUX_AUDIO */
52: #define BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_RX    0x0eu   /* DMA_V_REQ_MUX_AUDIO_RX */
53: #define BK7258_DMA_DEV_JPEG        0x19u   /* DMA_V_REQ_MUX_JPEG */
54: 
55: /* Transfer unit width, as encoded in ctrl.src_data_width/dest_data_width. */
56: 
57: #define BK7258_DMA_WIDTH_8BITS     0u
58: #define BK7258_DMA_WIDTH_16BITS    1u
59: #define BK7258_DMA_WIDTH_32BITS    2u
60: 
61: /****************************************************************************
62:  * Public Types
63:  ****************************************************************************/
64: 
65: typedef void (*bk7258_dma_done_cb_t)(void *arg);
66: 
67: /* One channel's configuration.
68:  *
69:  * dest_loop_start/dest_loop_end describe a circular destination and are
70:  * applied only when end > start; leave both zero for a linear write.  A
71:  * FIFO endpoint wants its *_inc false so the address stays put.
72:  */
73: 
74: struct bk7258_dma_cfg_s
75: {
76:   uint8_t  channel;
77:   uint32_t src_addr;
78:   uint32_t dest_addr;
79:   uint32_t transfer_len;      /* Bytes per finish interrupt. */
80:   uint8_t  src_dev;           /* BK7258_DMA_DEV_* request line. */
81:   uint8_t  dest_dev;
82:   bool     src_inc;
83:   bool     dest_inc;
84:   bool     repeat;            /* true = REPEAT, false = SINGLE. */
85:   uint32_t dest_loop_start;
86:   uint32_t dest_loop_end;
87:   uint8_t  data_width;        /* BK7258_DMA_WIDTH_*. */
88: };
89:

91:  * Public Function Prototypes
92:  ****************************************************************************/
93: 
94: void bk7258_dma_init(void);
95: 
96: /* Legacy single-shot memory-to-memory interface, channel 0. */
97: 
98: void bk7258_dma_configure(uint32_t src_addr, uint32_t dest_addr,
99:                            uint32_t transfer_len);
100: void bk7258_dma_set_done_callback(bk7258_dma_done_cb_t cb, void *arg);
101: void bk7258_dma_start(void);
102: void bk7258_dma_stop(void);
103: bool bk7258_dma_is_busy(void);
104: uint32_t bk7258_dma_get_remain_len(void);
105: 
106: /* General interface.  Returns 0, or -1 if the configuration is not
107:  * expressible (bad channel, zero or oversized length, bad width).
108:  */
109: 
110: int bk7258_dma_configure_ex(const struct bk7258_dma_cfg_s *cfg);
111: void bk7258_dma_set_channel_callback(uint8_t channel,
112:                                      bk7258_dma_done_cb_t cb, void *arg);
113: void bk7258_dma_start_channel(uint8_t channel);
114: void bk7258_dma_stop_channel(uint8_t channel);
115: uint32_t bk7258_dma_get_channel_remain_len(uint8_t channel);

118:  * Call before reading remain_len at the end of a peripheral-sourced
119:  * transfer, or the last few bytes are missed.  Safe from interrupt context:
120:  * the poll for completion is bounded.
121:  */

123: void bk7258_dma_flush_src_buffer(uint8_t channel);

15:  * be added there before playback can be handed to DMA.  At 16 kHz mono
16:  * the FIFO path is affordable; it will not be at 48 kHz stereo.
17:  *
18:  * Buffer completion is reported from a high-priority work queue rather

202: /****************************************************************************
203:  * Name: bk7258_audio_complete_work
204:  *
205:  * Description:
206:  *   Work-queue half of buffer completion.  Drains doneq and reports each
207:  *   buffer to the upper half.
208:  *
209:  ****************************************************************************/
210: 
211: static void bk7258_audio_complete_work(FAR void *arg)
212: {
213:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = arg;
214:   FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
215:   irqstate_t flags;
216: 
217:   for (; ; )
218:     {
219:       flags = enter_critical_section();
220:       apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_remfirst(&priv->doneq);
221:       leave_critical_section(flags);
222: 
223:       if (apb == NULL)
224:         {
225:           break;
226:         }
227: 
228: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
229:       priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK,
230:                       NULL);
231: #else
232:       priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK);
233: #endif
234:     }
235: }

237: /****************************************************************************
238:  * Name: bk7258_audio_finish
239:  *
240:  * Description:
241:  *   Move a finished buffer to doneq and schedule the completion work.
242:  *   Called from interrupt context.
243:  *
244:  ****************************************************************************/
245: 
246: static void bk7258_audio_finish(FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv,
247:                                 FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
248: {
249:   dq_addlast(&apb->dq_entry, &priv->doneq);
250: 
251:   if (work_available(&priv->work))
252:     {
253:       work_queue(HPWORK, &priv->work, bk7258_audio_complete_work, priv, 0);
254:     }
255: }

257: /****************************************************************************
258:  * Name: bk7258_audio_tx_callback
259:  *
260:  * Description:
261:  *   DAC FIFO service, invoked from the AUD ISR when the left FIFO has
262:  *   drained below its read threshold.
263:  *
264:  ****************************************************************************/
265: 
266: static void bk7258_audio_tx_callback(void *arg)
267: {
268:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = arg;
269:   FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
270:   unsigned int budget = BK7258_AUDIO_ISR_BUDGET;
271: 
272:   while (budget > 0)
273:     {
274:       apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_peek(&priv->pendq);
275:       if (apb == NULL)
276:         {
277:           /* Nothing left to play.  Mask the interrupt so the ISR does not
278:            * spin on a permanently-empty FIFO; enqueuebuffer() re-arms it.
279:            */
280: 
281:           bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(false);
282:           return;
283:         }
284: 
285:       if (apb->curbyte + sizeof(int16_t) <= apb->nbytes)
286:         {
287:           FAR const int16_t *samples =
288:             (FAR const int16_t *)(apb->samp + apb->curbyte);
289:           unsigned int avail = (apb->nbytes - apb->curbyte) /
290:                                sizeof(int16_t);
291:           unsigned int written;
292: 
293:           if (avail > budget)
294:             {
295:               avail = budget;
296:             }
297: 
298:           written = bk7258_aud_dac_write(samples, avail);
299:           apb->curbyte += written * sizeof(int16_t);
300:           budget -= written;
301: 
302:           if (written < avail)
303:             {
304:               /* FIFO is full: come back on the next interrupt. */
305: 
306:               return;
307:             }
308:         }
309:       else
310:         {
311:           /* Buffer exhausted (this also covers a zero-length buffer, which
312:            * the upper half uses to mark end of stream).
313:            */
314: 
315:           (void)dq_remfirst(&priv->pendq);
316:           bk7258_audio_finish(priv, apb);
317:         }
318:     }
319: }
320: 
321: /****************************************************************************
322:  * Name: bk7258_audio_rx_callback
323:  *
324:  * Description:
325:  *   ADC FIFO service, invoked from the AUD ISR when the FIFO has risen
326:  *   above its write threshold.
327:  *
328:  ****************************************************************************/
329: 
330: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE
331: static void bk7258_audio_rx_callback(void *arg)
332: {
333:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = arg;
334:   FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
335:   unsigned int budget = BK7258_AUDIO_ISR_BUDGET;
336: 
337:   while (budget > 0)
338:     {
339:       apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_peek(&priv->pendq);
340:       if (apb == NULL)
341:         {
342:           /* No buffer to fill.  Drop the interrupt rather than spinning;
343:            * the samples still in the FIFO are lost, which is the correct
344:            * behaviour for a capture overrun.
345:            */
346: 
347:           bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(false);
348:           return;
349:         }
350: 
351:       if (apb->nbytes + sizeof(int16_t) <= apb->nmaxbytes)
352:         {
353:           FAR int16_t *samples = (FAR int16_t *)(apb->samp + apb->nbytes);
354:           unsigned int room = (apb->nmaxbytes - apb->nbytes) /
355:                               sizeof(int16_t);
356:           unsigned int read;
357: 
358:           if (room > budget)
359:             {
360:               room = budget;
361:             }
362: 
363:           read = bk7258_aud_adc_read(samples, room);
364:           apb->nbytes += read * sizeof(int16_t);
365:           budget -= read;
366: 
367:           if (read < room)
368:             {
369:               /* FIFO drained: wait for the next interrupt. */
370: 
371:               return;
372:             }
373:         }
374:       else
375:         {
376:           (void)dq_remfirst(&priv->pendq);
377:           bk7258_audio_finish(priv, apb);
378:         }
379:     }
380: }
381: #endif

383: /****************************************************************************
384:  * Name: bk7258_audio_flush
385:  *
386:  * Description:
387:  *   Return every queued buffer to the upper half.  Used by shutdown and
388:  *   stop so no buffer is stranded in the lower half.
389:  *
390:  ****************************************************************************/
391: 
392: static void bk7258_audio_flush(FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv)
393: {
394:   FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
395:   irqstate_t flags;
396: 
397:   for (; ; )
398:     {
399:       flags = enter_critical_section();
400:       apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_remfirst(&priv->pendq);
401:       leave_critical_section(flags);
402: 
403:       if (apb == NULL)
404:         {
405:           break;
406:         }
407: 
408: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
409:       priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK,
410:                       NULL);
411: #else
412:       priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK);
413: #endif
414:     }
415: 
416:   bk7258_audio_complete_work(priv);
417: }

419: /****************************************************************************
420:  * Name: bk7258_audio_poll_adc
421:  *
422:  * Description:
423:  *   Diagnostic helper: drain the ADC FIFO by polling for roughly 200 ms,
424:  *   deliberately ignoring the interrupt path.  Returns the sample count and
425:  *   accumulates the sum of squares so the caller can report a mean square.
426:  *
427:  ****************************************************************************/
428: 
429: static unsigned int bk7258_audio_poll_adc(FAR uint64_t *sumsq)
430: {
431:   int16_t samples[32];
432:   unsigned int total = 0;
433:   unsigned int i;
434: 
435:   for (i = 0; i < 200; i++)
436:     {
437:       unsigned int got = bk7258_aud_adc_read(samples, 32);
438:       unsigned int j;
439: 
440:       for (j = 0; j < got; j++)
441:         {
442:           *sumsq += (uint64_t)((int32_t)samples[j] * (int32_t)samples[j]);
443:         }
444: 
445:       total += got;
446:       up_udelay(1000);
447:     }
448: 
449:   return total;
450: }

452: /****************************************************************************
453:  * Name: bk7258_audio_getcaps
454:  ****************************************************************************/
455: 
456: static int bk7258_audio_getcaps(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, int type,
457:                                 FAR struct audio_caps_s *caps)
458: {
459:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
460: 
461:   (void)type;
462: 
463:   DEBUGASSERT(caps != NULL &&
464:               caps->ac_len >= sizeof(struct audio_caps_s));
465: 
466:   caps->ac_format.hw  = 0;
467:   caps->ac_controls.w = 0;
468: 
469:   switch (caps->ac_type)
470:     {
471:       case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:
472: 
473:         /* Playback is mono: the chip has no right DAC and the board has a
474:          * single speaker.  Capture reports two channels when the MIC2 echo
475:          * reference is enabled, because frames really are L/R interleaved
476:          * (L = voice, R = reference) even though only one of the two is a
477:          * microphone.
478:          */
479: 
480:         caps->ac_channels = priv->playback ? 1 :
481:                             (priv->cfg.capture_reference ? 2 : 1);
482: 
483:         switch (caps->ac_subtype)
484:           {
485:             case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:
486:               caps->ac_controls.b[0] = priv->playback ? AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT :
487:                                                         AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT;
488:               caps->ac_format.hw = 1 << (AUDIO_FMT_PCM - 1);
489:               break;
490: 
491:             default:
492:               caps->ac_controls.b[0] = AUDIO_SUBFMT_END;
493:               break;
494:           }
495:         break;
496: 
497:       case AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT:
498:       case AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT:
499:         caps->ac_channels = priv->playback ? 1 :
500:                             (priv->cfg.capture_reference ? 2 : 1);
501: 
502:         switch (caps->ac_subtype)
503:           {
504:             case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:
505: 
506:               /* Only the rates reachable from the 26 MHz crystal are
507:                * advertised.  The 44.1k/48k families additionally need the
508:                * APLL calibration sequence, which aud_clk_config() in
509:                * bk7258_aud.c deliberately rejects with -ENOTSUP until it
510:                * has been transcribed from the vendor tree.
511:                */
512: 
513:               caps->ac_controls.hw[0] = AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_8K |
514:                                         AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_16K |
515:                                         AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_32K;
516:               caps->ac_controls.b[2] = 16;   /* Bits per sample */
517:               break;
518: 
519:             default:
520:               break;
521:           }
522:         break;
523: 
524:       default:
525:         caps->ac_subtype = 0;
526:         caps->ac_channels = 0;
527:         break;
528:     }
529: 
530:   return caps->ac_len;
531: }

533: /****************************************************************************
534:  * Name: bk7258_audio_configure
535:  ****************************************************************************/
536: 
537: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
538: static int bk7258_audio_configure(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
539:                                   FAR void *session,
540:                                   FAR const struct audio_caps_s *caps)
541: #else
542: static int bk7258_audio_configure(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
543:                                   FAR const struct audio_caps_s *caps)
544: #endif
545: {
546:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
547:   uint32_t samplerate;
548:   int ret;
549: 
550: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
551:   (void)session;
552: #endif
553: 
554:   DEBUGASSERT(caps != NULL);
555: 
556:   switch (caps->ac_type)
557:     {
558:       case AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT:
559:       case AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT:
560:         if ((caps->ac_type == AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT) != priv->playback)
561:           {
562:             return -EINVAL;
563:           }
564: 
565:         /* Sample width.  The FIFO ports are 16 bits per sample and the
566:          * copy loops below step by sizeof(int16_t), so anything else would
567:          * be silently misinterpreted rather than merely sounding wrong.
568:          */
569: 
570:         if (caps->ac_controls.b[2] != 0 && caps->ac_controls.b[2] != 16)
571:           {
572:             auderr("unsupported sample width %u\n",
573:                    caps->ac_controls.b[2]);
574:             return -EINVAL;
575:           }
576: 
577:         /* Channel count.  Playback is mono because the chip has no right
578:          * DAC.  Capture is two channels when the MIC2 echo reference is
579:          * enabled and one otherwise; the count is a property of the
580:          * hardware wiring, not something the caller can choose.
581:          */
582: 
583:         if (caps->ac_channels != 0)
584:           {
585:             uint8_t expected = priv->playback ? 1 :
586:                                (priv->cfg.capture_reference ? 2 : 1);
587: 
588:             if (caps->ac_channels != expected)
589:               {
590:                 auderr("unsupported channel count %u, expected %u\n",
591:                        caps->ac_channels, expected);
592:                 return -EINVAL;
593:               }
594:           }
595: 
596:         /* nxplayer splits the sample rate across hw[0] and b[3] (see
597:          * nxplayer.c:1935-1936), so both halves have to be recombined.
598:          */
599: 
600:         samplerate = caps->ac_controls.hw[0] |
601:                      ((uint32_t)caps->ac_controls.b[3] << 16);
602:         if (samplerate != 0)
603:           {
604:             priv->cfg.samplerate = samplerate;
605:           }
606: 
607:         if (priv->playback)
608:           {
609:             ret = bk7258_aud_dac_setup(&priv->cfg);
610:           }
611:         else
612:           {
613:             ret = bk7258_aud_adc_setup(&priv->cfg);
614:           }
615: 
616:         if (ret < 0)
617:           {
618:             auderr("%s setup failed: %d\n",
619:                    priv->playback ? "DAC" : "ADC", ret);
620:             return ret;
621:           }
622: 
623:         priv->configured = true;
624:         break;
625: 
626:       case AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE:
627: 
628:         /* Volume maps onto the DAC's digital gain.  The upper half passes
629:          * 0..1000; scale that onto 0..0x3f, whose 0 dB point is 0x2d.
630:          */
631: 
632: #ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_VOLUME
633:         if (caps->ac_format.hw == AUDIO_FU_VOLUME && priv->playback)
634:           {
635:             uint16_t volume = caps->ac_controls.hw[0];
636:             uint8_t gain;
637: 
638:             if (volume > 1000)
639:               {
640:                 volume = 1000;
641:               }
642: 
643:             gain = (uint8_t)((volume * BK7258_AUD_DAC_DIG_GAIN_MAX) / 1000);
644:             return bk7258_aud_dac_set_dig_gain(gain);
645:           }
646: 
647: #endif
648:         return -ENOTTY;
649: 
650:       default:
651:         return -ENOTTY;
652:     }
653: 
654:   return OK;
655: }

687: /****************************************************************************
688:  * Name: bk7258_audio_start
689:  *
690:  * Description:
691:  *   Playback start-up order follows the vendor's onboard_speaker_stream
692:  *   implementation (aud_dac start, pa_on_delay, amplifier on, un-mute):
693:  *   the amplifier stays muted while the DAC's analog output settles, so
694:  *   the speaker does not pop.  R71's 10K pull-down keeps CTRL low until
695:  *   bk7258_audio_pa_enable(true) drives it, which means the hardware is
696:  *   already silent before software gets here.
697:  *
698:  ****************************************************************************/
699: 
700: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
701: static int bk7258_audio_start(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
702:                               FAR void *session)
703: #else
704: static int bk7258_audio_start(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
705: #endif
706: {
707:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
708: 
709: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
710:   (void)session;
711: #endif
712: 
713:   if (!priv->configured)
714:     {
715:       return -EPERM;
716:     }
717: 
718:   if (priv->running)
719:     {
720:       return OK;
721:     }
722: 
723:   if (priv->playback)
724:     {
725:       bk7258_aud_set_tx_callback(bk7258_audio_tx_callback, priv);
726:       bk7258_aud_dac_start();
727: 
728:       nxsig_usleep(CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_PA_ON_DELAY_MS * 1000);
729: 
730:       bk7258_audio_pa_enable(true);
731:       bk7258_aud_dac_mute(false);
732: 
733:       bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(true);
734:     }
735: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE
736:   else
737:     {
738:       bk7258_aud_set_rx_callback(bk7258_audio_rx_callback, priv);
739:       bk7258_aud_adc_start();
740:       bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(true);
741:     }
742: #endif
743: 
744:   priv->running = true;
745:   priv->paused = false;
746: 
747:   return OK;
748: }

750: /****************************************************************************
751:  * Name: bk7258_audio_stop
752:  *
753:  * Description:
754:  *   Teardown order is the inverse and is deliberately mute-first.  Note
755:  *   the vendor's own header and code disagree about where pa_off_delay
756:  *   sits: onboard_speaker_stream.h:51 describes it as the delay *after*
757:  *   turning the amplifier off, while onboard_speaker_stream.c:341-345
758:  *   sleeps *before* pulling the GPIO low.  The code order is the one that
759:  *   actually lets the analog output settle while still muted, so that is
760:  *   what is implemented here.
761:  *
762:  ****************************************************************************/
763: 
764: #ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_STOP
765: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
766: static int bk7258_audio_stop(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
767:                              FAR void *session)
768: #else
769: static int bk7258_audio_stop(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
770: #endif
771: {
772:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
773: 
774: #ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
775:   (void)session;
776: #endif
777: 
778:   if (priv->playback)
779:     {
780:       bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(false);
781: 
782:       bk7258_aud_dac_mute(true);
783:       nxsig_usleep(CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_PA_OFF_DELAY_MS * 1000);
784:       bk7258_audio_pa_enable(false);
785: 
786:       bk7258_aud_dac_stop();
787:     }
788:   else
789:     {
790:       bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(false);
791:       bk7258_aud_adc_stop();
792:     }
793: 
794:   if (priv->playback)
795:     {
796:       bk7258_aud_set_tx_callback(NULL, NULL);
797:     }
798:   else
799:     {
800:       bk7258_aud_set_rx_callback(NULL, NULL);
801:     }
802: 
803:   priv->running = false;
804:   priv->paused = false;
805: 
806:   bk7258_audio_flush(priv);
807: 
808:   return OK;
809: }
810: #endif

812: /****************************************************************************
813:  * Name: bk7258_audio_pause / bk7258_audio_resume
814:  *
815:  * Description:
816:  *   Pause only masks the FIFO interrupt and mutes; the DAC stays enabled
817:  *   and the amplifier stays on so resume is click-free.
818:  *

952: static int bk7258_audio_ioctl(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
953:                               unsigned long arg)
954: {
955:   FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
956: 
957:   (void)priv;
958: 
959:   switch (cmd)
960:     {
961:       /* This must be answered unconditionally, and NOT hidden behind
962:        * CONFIG_AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS.
963:        *
964:        * The upper half latches its buffer quota from this call:
965:        * audio.c:1267-1279 forwards GETBUFFERINFO to the lower half and only
966:        * assigns upper->nbuffers when the lower half returns >= 0.  If the
967:        * lower half answers -ENOTTY, upper->nbuffers stays 0, and then
968:        * audio_allocbuffer() (audio.c:786-789) short-circuits with
969:        * "return 0" on the very first AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER because
970:        * periods >= nbuffers already holds.  The application then cannot
971:        * obtain a single buffer, which is what "ALLOCBUFFER 0 failed: 0"
972:        * looked like on hardware.
973:        */
974: 
975:       case AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:
976:         {
977:           FAR struct ap_buffer_info_s *bufinfo =
978:             (FAR struct ap_buffer_info_s *)arg;
979: 
980:           if (bufinfo == NULL)
981:             {
982:               return -EINVAL;
983:             }
984: 
985:           bufinfo->buffer_size = CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES;
986:           bufinfo->nbuffers    = CONFIG_AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS;
987:         }
988:         break;
989: 
990:       /* Diagnostic: dump registers, then read the FIFO by polling so the
991:        * interrupt path is taken out of the picture entirely.
992:        */
993: 
994:       case BK7258_AUDIOIOC_DIAG:
995:         {
996:           unsigned int total = 0;
997:           uint64_t sumsq = 0;
998:           unsigned int i;
999: 
1000:           syslog(LOG_INFO, "diag: %s, configured=%d running=%d "
1001:                  "paused=%d rate=%" PRIu32 " ref=%d\n",
1002:                  priv->playback ? "playback" : "capture",
1003:                  priv->configured, priv->running, priv->paused,
1004:                  priv->cfg.samplerate, priv->cfg.capture_reference);
1005: 
1006:           bk7258_aud_dump();
1007: 
1008:           if (!priv->playback)
1009:             {
1010:               bool forced;
1011: 
1012:               forced = bk7258_aud_force_module_clock();
1013:               syslog(LOG_INFO, "diag: aud_cken was %s\n",
1014:                      forced ? "CLEAR -> now set by AP" : "already set");
1015: 
1016:               /* Which MIC front end actually reaches the ADC?
1017:                *
1018:                * The ADC has been measured to deliver a single channel, so
1019:                * the right half of every FIFO word is always zero and MIC2
1020:                * never shows up in a normal capture.  Looking at MIC2 on
1021:                * its own is the only way to tell whether the board's
1022:                * post-amplifier echo tap (HT6872 OUT+/OUT- -> R84/R83 ->
1023:                * C61/C60 -> MIC2P/MIC2N) carries signal at all, which is a
1024:                * board-level question rather than a driver one.
1025:                */
1026: 
1027:               bk7258_aud_select_mic(true, false);
1028:               up_udelay(5000);
1029:               sumsq = 0;
1030:               total = bk7258_audio_poll_adc(&sumsq);
1031:               syslog(LOG_INFO,
1032:                      "diag: MIC1 only -> %u samples, meansq=%llu\n", total,
1033:                      total ? (unsigned long long)(sumsq / total) : 0ull);
1034: 
1035:               bk7258_aud_select_mic(false, true);
1036:               up_udelay(5000);
1037:               sumsq = 0;
1038:               total = bk7258_audio_poll_adc(&sumsq);
1039:               syslog(LOG_INFO,
1040:                      "diag: MIC2 only -> %u samples, meansq=%llu\n", total,
1041:                      total ? (unsigned long long)(sumsq / total) : 0ull);
1042: 
1043:               /* Leave MIC1 selected again. */
1044: 
1045:               bk7258_aud_select_mic(true, priv->cfg.capture_reference);
1046: 
1047:               /* AUD_CLK_CONTROL sweep.
1048:                *
1049:                * Only bit0 (ADC_SOFT_RESET) and bit1 (ADC_CLK_GATE) exist,
1050:                * so all four combinations can simply be tried in order,
1051:                * polling after each.  This settles by experiment what the
1052:                * vendor sources describe inconsistently: whether bit0 is a
1053:                * pulse that must be cleared (this driver's current
1054:                * behaviour) or a release that must stay asserted (what
1055:                * bk_aud_driver_init() actually leaves behind).
1056:                */
1057: 
1058:               for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
1059:                 {
1060:                   bk7258_aud_set_clk_control(i);
1061:                   up_udelay(2000);
1062: 
1063:                   sumsq = 0;
1064:                   total = bk7258_audio_poll_adc(&sumsq);
1065: 
1066:                   syslog(LOG_INFO,
1067:                          "diag: clkctl=0x%x (rst=%d gate=%d) -> %u samples,"
1068:                          " meansq=%llu fifosta=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n",
1069:                          i, i & 1, (i >> 1) & 1, total,
1070:                          total ? (unsigned long long)(sumsq / total) : 0ull,
1071:                          bk7258_aud_fifo_status());
1072:                 }
1073:             }
1074: 
1075:           syslog(LOG_INFO, "diag: fifo status after poll=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n",
1076:                  bk7258_aud_fifo_status());
1077:         }
1078:         break;
1079: 
1080:       default:
1081:         (void)arg;
1082:         return -ENOTTY;
1083:     }
1084: 
1085:   return OK;
1086: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_audio_bringup.c
3:  *
4:  * Registration glue for the internal-DAC audio path, plus ownership of the
5:  * one piece of board wiring the chip layer must not know about: the
6:  * HT6872 amplifier's mute GPIO.
7:  *
8:  * Board facts this file encodes (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf):
9:  *
10:  *   - Net MUTE is BK7258 P50 (the sheet 2/6 chip pin table lists it
11:  *     against "P50/ENET_RXD1/R0"), reaching the HT6872's CTRL pin through
12:  *     R70 (1K).  R71 (10K) pulls CTRL to ground, so the amplifier is
13:  *     muted at power-on and stays muted until software drives P50 high --
14:  *     which is what suppresses the classic boot pop.
15:  *   - The amplifier is supplied from PA_VDD, which comes from VBAT, not
16:  *     from the LDO_3V3 rail gated by LDO33_EN.  Audio therefore does not
17:  *     depend on that rail's enable.
18:  *
19:  * A note on the GPIO number, because the same reasoning already cost this
20:  * project repeated camera bring-up failures: GPIO50's name in the vendor
21:  * pinmux table is ENET_RXD1 (gpio_map.h:78), which says nothing about what
22:  * the board actually connects it to.  Only the schematic net name does --
23:  * here PA_SD, reaching the HT6872 CTRL pin through R70.  The camera's
24:  * control bus went through the same correction; see the file header of
25:  * chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_gc2145_i2c_bitbang.h for that write-up.
26:  *
27:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
28:  ****************************************************************************/
29:

31:  * Included Files
32:  ****************************************************************************/
33:

39: #include <stdio.h>

89: int bk7258_audio_initialize(void)
90: {
91:   FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *lower;
92:   int ret;
93: 
94:   /* Park the amplifier in its muted state before anything else touches
95:    * the audio path.  Configuring the pad as an output-low both takes it
96:    * off LCD_R0 and makes the R71 pull-down's intent explicit rather than
97:    * relying on the pad staying an input.
98:    */
99: 
100:   bk7258_gpio_output(BK7258_AUDIO_PA_GPIO, false);
101: 
102:   ret = bk7258_aud_initialize();
103:   if (ret < 0)
104:     {
105:       printf("bk7258_audio: AUD block bring-up failed, error=%d\n", ret);
106:       return ret;
107:     }
108: 
109:   printf("bk7258_audio: AUD id=0x%08lx version=0x%08lx, PA mute on GPIO%u\n",
110:          (unsigned long)bk7258_aud_read_id(),
111:          (unsigned long)bk7258_aud_read_version(),
112:          BK7258_AUDIO_PA_GPIO);

114:   lower = bk7258_audio_dev_initialize(true);
115:   if (lower == NULL)
116:     {
117:       return -ENODEV;
118:     }
119: 
120:   ret = audio_register("pcm0p", lower);

122:     {
123:       printf("bk7258_audio: failed to register /dev/audio/pcm0p, "
124:              "error=%d\n", ret);
125:       return ret;
126:     }
127: 
128:   printf("bk7258_audio: /dev/audio/pcm0p registered (internal DAC -> "
129:          "HT6872)\n");

131: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE
132:   lower = bk7258_audio_dev_initialize(false);
133:   if (lower == NULL)
134:     {
135:       return -ENODEV;
136:     }
137:

139:   if (ret < 0)
140:     {
141:       printf("bk7258_audio: failed to register /dev/audio/pcm0c, "
142:              "error=%d\n", ret);

---

## Comprehensive DMA-Related Code and Configuration Summary

### 1. MCU Architecture

**Target SoC:** Beken BK7258  
**CPU Core:** ARM Cortex-M33 (ARMv8-M architecture with TrustZone)  
- `CONFIG_ARCH_ARM=y`
- `CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV8M=y`

- CPU Freq: 480 MHz (ai_agent config) or 120 MHz (basic nsh config)

---

### 2. DMA Controller Hardware Details

The BK7258 has a **general-purpose DMA (GDMA)** controller at base address `0x45020000`, documented in the following key files:

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_dma.c` | **Low-level DMA driver** (473 lines) - Register definitions, init, configure, start/stop, callbacks, interrupt handler |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_dma.h` | **DMA driver header** - API declarations, constants |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/dma/dma.h` | **NuttX generic DMA API** - The `dma_dev_s`, `dma_chan_s`, `dma_ops_s` structs and DMA macros (`DMA_GET_CHAN`, `DMA_START`, `DMA_START_CYCLIC`, etc.) |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/audio/audio_dma.c` | **NuttX audio DMA bridge** - Generic audio lower-half driver using the DMA API |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/boards/arm/cxd56xx/drivers/audio/cxd56_audio_dma.c`, `.h` | **CXD56 audio DMA driver** (reference for another ARM board) |

**DMA Controller Capabilities:**
- **12 DMA channels** (`BK7258_DMA_NCHANNELS = 12u`)
- Base address: `0x45020000` (`SOC_GENER_DMA_REG_BASE`)
- Channel group stride: `0x40` (16 words per channel)
- Support for **SINGLE** and **REPEAT** modes
- Support for **circular destination** (loop mode)
- **Peripheral request lines** (req_mux encodings):
  - `BK7258_DMA_DEV_MEM` = `0x00` (memory)
  - `BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_TX` = `0x0d` (audio DAC/TX)
  - `BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_RX` = `0x0e` (audio ADC/RX)
  - `BK7258_DMA_DEV_JPEG` = `0x19` (JPEG encoder)
- Data widths: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit
- Interrupt-driven with per-channel finish interrupt

**Vendor SDK DMA Files** (bk_idk/bk_avdk_smp):
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/general_dma/v1px/dma_driver.c` | V1 DMA driver |

### 3. Camera Drivers and DMA Usage

**Camera subsystem files:**

| File | Description |

| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_camera_imgdata.h` | Camera imgdata header |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_camera_imgsensor.c` | **GC2145 sensor driver** (imgsensor half) - I2C programming, power/reset, DVP pinmux, MCLK |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_camera_bringup.c` | Camera bringup/registration glue |

| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_jpeg_enc.c` | JPEG encoder driver |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_gc2145_i2c_bitbang.c` | Bit-banged I2C for GC2145 |

**Camera DMA Usage:**
The camera uses DMA for **JPEG capture**. The JPEG encoder outputs bitstream through a FIFO register (not memory-mapped), so a DMA channel must drain it.

Key points from the code (`bk7258_camera_imgdata.c`):
- JPEG capture uses DMA channel 0 (`BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_DMA_CH = 0`)
- DMA configured in **REPEAT mode** with **circular destination** - one configuration absorbs a whole frame
- Source: JPEG encoder FIFO (`src_dev = BK7258_DMA_DEV_JPEG`, `src_inc = false`)
- Destination: V4L2 buffer in PSRAM (`dest_dev = BK7258_DMA_DEV_MEM`, `dest_inc = true`)
- Transfer chunk size: 10KB (`BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_CHUNK`)
- Data width: 32 bits
- Functions used: `bk7258_dma_configure_ex()`, `bk7258_dma_start_channel()`, `bk7258_dma_stop_channel()`, `bk7258_dma_flush_src_buffer()`
- The YUV (raw) path does **NOT** use DMA - YUV_BUF writes directly into the frame buffer in PSRAM

**Camera config (defconfig):**
- `CONFIG_DRIVERS_VIDEO=y`
- `CONFIG_VIDEO=y`
- `CONFIG_VIDEO_FB=y`
- `CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM=y`
- `CONFIG_SYSTEM_NXCAMERA=y`
- `CONFIG_BK7258_JPEG_ENC=y`
- `CONFIG_LIBYUV=y`
- `CONFIG_LIB_JPEG_TURBO=y`

The camera sensor is **GalaxyCore GC2145** (2MP, 1600x1200 max, configured at 640x480 default), connected via DVP parallel interface with bit-banged I2C control.

### 4. Audio Drivers and DMA Usage

**Audio subsystem files:**

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_audio_dev.c` | **Audio lower-half driver** (1182 lines) - DAC playback + ADC capture via interrupt-driven FIFO |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_audio_bringup.c` | Audio bringup/registration |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_aud.c` | Chip-layer audio HAL |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/audio/audio_dma.c` | **NuttX generic DMA-based audio driver** (611 lines) - Uses NuttX DMA API |
| `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/audio/audio_dma.h` | Audio DMA header |

**Audio DMA Usage:**
The BK7258 audio driver currently uses **interrupt-driven FIFO copy** (NOT DMA), as explicitly stated in the code comments:
> "The chip's DMA engine is not used yet: bk7258_dma.c currently exposes a single-instance memory-to-memory channel (bk7258_dma_configure/start/stop with no channel argument), so a peripheral-destination circular channel has to be added there before playback can be handed to DMA"

However, the DMA request lines are defined and ready:
- `BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_TX = 0x0d` (for playback DMA)
- `BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_RX = 0x0e` (for capture DMA)

The generic `audio_dma.c` in NuttX provides a ready-to-use DMA-based audio driver using `audio_dma_initialize()` with a `dma_dev_s` device.

I2S peripheral drivers exist in the vendor SDK but are not yet integrated into the NuttX BK7258 board:

- Playback registered as `/dev/audio/pcm0p`
- Capture registered as `/dev/audio/pcm0c`

Audio is connected to an **HT6872 amplifier** on `GPIO50` (mute control).

### 5. Other DMA Users

- **UART DMA**: UART TX/RX DMA is configurable in Kconfig (`CONFIG_UART_TX_DMA`, `CONFIG_UART_RX_DMA`) but not enabled in the current BK7258 defconfigs

The project uses minimal Device Tree files. The BK7258 is a custom board under NuttX that does **not** use Device Tree for its hardware description (it uses `CONFIG_ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM` + chip-level C code). The only .dts/.dtsi files found are for other platforms:

### 8. Summary of DMA Flow in the Project

```
BK7258 DMA Controller (12 channels, 0x45020000 base)
   |
   |-- Channel 0 (BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_DMA_CH)
   |     Used by: Camera JPEG Capture (imgdata driver)
   |     Mode: REPEAT + circular destination
   |     Source: JPEG encoder FIFO (BK7258_DMA_DEV_JPEG, req_mux 0x19)
   |     Destination: PSRAM V4L2 buffer
   |     Chunk: 10KB, Width: 32-bit
   |
   |-- Channel ? (BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_TX, req_mux 0x0d)
   |     Defined but NOT YET USED - audio currently uses interrupt-driven FIFO
   |     The generic audio_dma.c driver is available for this purpose
   |
   |-- Channel ? (BK7258_DMA_DEV_AUDIO_RX, req_mux 0x0e)
   |     Defined but NOT YET USED - audio capture uses interrupt-driven FIFO
   |
   |-- UART DMA channels
   |     Configurable in Kconfig but NOT enabled in current defconfigs
   |
   |-- SDIO DMA
   |     Explicitly disabled: # CONFIG_SDIO_DMA is not set
```

**NuttX Generic DMA Infrastructure:**
- `include/nuttx/dma/dma.h` defines the abstract DMA API (`dma_dev_s`, `dma_chan_s`, `dma_ops_s`)
- `drivers/dma/` contains the generic DMA framework
- `drivers/audio/audio_dma.c` bridges the DMA API to the audio subsystem
- The BK7258 uses its own custom DMA driver (`bk7258_dma.c`) rather than the NuttX generic DMA framework for JPEG capture
- For audio, the code comments indicate that the generic `audio_dma_initialize()` could be used once the DMA driver supports peripheral channels
